summary.title: Chapter 8 - On-Call (SRE Workbook)
summary.one_liner: Learn how Google SRE teams structure on-call rotations, reduce pager load, and ramp up new engineers, with real examples from Google and Evernote.
takeaways: On-call means being available for a set period and responding to production incidents, with SREs also handling nonurgent production duties.
Google targets at most two incidents per on-call shift and at least 50% of SRE time on project work, to keep on-call sustainable.
A new team can ramp up for on-call using a checklist of focus areas, deep-dive sessions, lab practice, 'Wheel of Misfortune' role-play, and shadowing before becoming primary.
Evernote classified alerts as P1 (page now), P2 (next business day), and P3 (informational), tying paging to SLO impact.
High pager load is diagnosed by comparing pages per shift to a pager budget; symptom-based, SLO-aligned alerts help reduce noise.
summary.summary: This is the Chapter 8 of the Google SRE Workbook, which revisits on-call practice after the first SRE book. It answers common questions from smaller teams about mixed developer and DevOps rotations, high page volumes, and turnover. It walks through example setups: a Google SRE team that was formed in Mountain View and ramped up for on-call within three months, and Evernote's move to Google Cloud with a reworked alerting and triage process. The page also explains what drives pager load and begins a case study of an overloaded team with a pager budget of two pages per shift.
